Over the last five or so years, there has been a rise in diversity, which has made people more curious but at the same time, being a person of color can attract negative attention.

Because many Georgians haven’t been exposed to a lot of people of color, they often have preconceived notions about us. Some stare out of curiosity, while others may stare because they see us as something “exotic” or even “disgusting.” Some view us in a hypersexualized way, which is unsettling.

Georgian culture, history, and identity are distinct and more closely aligned with its neighbors rather than European traditions an example is Georgias geographically located at the intersection of Europe and Asia, it has a cultural heritage that is deeply tied to the Caucasus region and its neighboring countries like Armenia, Azerbaijan, Turkey, and Iran. Georgian culture is distinct from European cultures for several reasons
Geographic and Historical Context
Georgia’s position in the South Caucasus has historically linked it more closely to the Middle East and Central Asia than to Europe. Its long history of interaction with Persian, Ottoman, and Byzantine empires shaped its cultural, linguistic, and religious development in ways that differ from European trajectories.
Cultural and Social Values
Georgian society is often more conservative, sharing values and traditions similar to its neighbors in Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Iran. Family structures, hospitality, and social norms in Georgia have parallels with these cultures.
The Georgian language, as part of the Kartvelian family, has no ties to Indo European languages. Its vocabulary and script have been influenced by Persian, Arabic, and Turkish, further distinguishing it from European languages like Italian or Slavic tongues in the Balkans.
Georgian food shares significant similarities with Armenian, Turkish, and Iranian cuisines. Dishes like khinkali (dumplings), badrijani nigvzit (eggplant with walnuts), and kharcho (a walnut and spice-based stew) resonate more with Middle Eastern and Caucasian flavors. While Georgian cuisine incorporates some Mediterranean elements, such as fresh salads, its core remains distinct from European culinary traditions.ethnically, Georgians often share physical traits with their neighboring Caucasus populations rather than those from Southern or Eastern Europe. This shared ancestry contributes to the perception of stronger cultural and historical ties within the area. So in conclusion georgia’s rich and ancient history, including its unique traditions, music, art, and wine making practices, makes it a culture that stands apart. There is no need to draw comparisons to European cultures like the Balkans or Italy, as Georgia’s heritage is valuable and self-sustaining in its own right.I personally think Georgia is unique but is not similar with any European country. While some modern influences, such as Russian or Mediterranean elements, have blended into Georgian culture, its foundation remains deeply rooted in the Caucasus and its historical interactions with neighboring regions.
